title: Cryo-nerve blockade for perioperative pain relief during sternotomy in cardiac surgery
summary: In the majority of the cases, patients of cardiac surgeries undergo sternotomy, which means the breast bone is cut open during surgery . This causes pain symptoms that, on the one hand, reduce perioperative patient comfort, but on the other hand also have a direct influence on recovery and an increase in perioperative morbidity. Overall, pain and medical pain treatment potentially lead to reduced mobilization and prolonged intensive care treatment. In addition to increasing morbidity, pain also directly influences the quality of life of those treated. Through a medium-term effective blockade of intercostal nerves through cryoablation, the multimodal scheme used so far could be modified so that, on the one hand, less pain and pain-related complications occur, and on the other hand, there is less need for painkillers and fewer painkiller-related complications. In this study we include patients undergoing sternotomy comparing the postperative pain relief with and without intercostal cryoablation. Included are all suitable patients undergoing coronary bypass and / or aortic valve procedures via full sternotomy with and without cryo nerve blockade.

interventions.name: 50 patients receiving sternotomy with painkiller treatment and cryo-nerve blockade
control group 50 patients receiving sternotomy with painkiller treatment but without cryo-nerve blockade

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
all-comers patients undergoing coronary bypass and / or aortic valve
procedures via full sternotomy
Exclusion criteria:
Patients younger than 18 years
Patients with thoracic or pectoral malformations (i.e. pectus excavatum, kyphosis)
Patients with known painkiller abuse or opioid abuse
Patients with painkiller allergies
Patients with combination procedures
Patients unable to give informed written consent
Patients with contraindications to painbuster intake
Patients unable to take part in telephone follow ups
Patients with lactation or pregnancy
Patients with COPD Gold III or IV
